newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rules out foreign investigation of polls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rules out foreign investigation of polls.

text.p: The Indonesian government said foreign observers invited to monitor the country's May 29 general elections would not be allowed to investigate or pass judgement, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Saturday.

"We are letting foreigners come to see how the election proceeds, but it is our right to judge the election," Soetojo, director-general of sociopolitical affairs at the Interior Ministry, was quoted as saying on Friday.
"We did not do anything but watch when we were invited by governments of neighbouring countries to observe their elections," he added.

Interior Minister Yogie Memet said last week that Indonesia would invite neighbouring and other countries to monitor the election to be contested by the ruling Golkar party and the two minorities parties, the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and the United Development Party (PPP)

It will be Indonesia's first election to be monitored by foreign observers. The Jakarta Post said the decision appeared to be a compromise to the two minority parties which have complained about irregularities in the past elections.
Soetojo said the foreigners would be considered to be meddling in Indonesia's internal affairs if they went beyond the granted privilege of observing the polls.

He said the government was completing the registration of invitees, who are likely to come from Southeast Asian countries. "Not all countries will be invited, but Malaysia, Singapore and our other neighbours will be for sure," he said.

Soetojo said the government would give free access to observers to monitor the various stages of the election, especially the voting, but only to foreigners who had received formal invitations. The paper gave no further details.

Police have slapped bans on street parades and restricted public gatherings ahead of the elections, while broadcasts on state television and radio must be checked by government officials before going to air.
